overview.headline: DNA stores hereditary instructions in a double helix

keyPoints.point: DNA is the hereditary material shared by humans and most other organisms.
keyPoints.quote: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.

keyPoints.point: Information in DNA is stored as a code using four chemical bases.
keyPoints.quote: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).

keyPoints.point: Nucleotides arranged in two long strands form a spiral double helix.
keyPoints.quote: Nucleotides are arranged in two long strands that form a spiral called a double helix.

keyPoints.point: DNA can replicate to make copies so new cells receive exact sequences.
keyPoints.quote: An important property of DNA is that it can replicate, or make copies of itself.

keyTerms.gloss: DNA located in the cell nucleus that holds most hereditary material
keyTerms.quote: Most DNA is located in the cell nucleus (where it is called nuclear DNA)

keyTerms.gloss: Small amount of DNA found in mitochondria outside the nucleus
keyTerms.quote: but a small amount of DNA can also be found in the mitochondria (where it is called mitochondrial DNA or mtDNA).

keyTerms.gloss: Units of paired bases where A joins T and C joins G
keyTerms.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyTerms.gloss: Building unit made of a base with sugar and phosphate
keyTerms.quote: Together, a base, sugar, and phosphate are called a nucleotide.

keyTerms.gloss: Spiral of two long strands held together by base pairs
keyTerms.quote: Nucleotides are arranged in two long strands that form a spiral called a double helix.
